The Lead · Frontier

Anthropic’s IPO Order Book Reached Six Times the Shares on Offer by Thursday

Investors had ordered six times the shares Anthropic is selling by Thursday night, Reuters reports — for a $64 billion offering, demand bankers call strong. The same investors are asking whether the company can hold its lead. Wednesday’s price is where the two facts meet.

Read the lead →

No. 027 · Saturday, November 14, 2026

Today in 30 Seconds

  • The book is six times full. Anthropic’s IPO drew orders for six times the shares on offer by Thursday night, for a $64 billion sale that prices on Wednesday.
  • The first name for Nvidia’s top job. The board has sounded out Arm’s Rene Haas about succeeding Jensen Huang, reports say; Nvidia calls the speculation premature.
  • $74 billion, two votes. SpaceX pledged two AI campuses in Texas and Arizona; both face local decisions on December 9, and neither is approved.
  • Every departure, stopped. A communications failure led the FAA to halt all departing flights in the United States for more than four hours on Friday.
  • Fake stores in the answers. Chatbots pointed shoppers at risky retail sites in up to 15% of shopping answers in a 151-brand test, weeks before Black Friday.

The Position

The paper’s argument

Six Times Subscribed Is a Queue, Not a Verdict on the Price

Six times subscribed sounds like a verdict. It is a queue. Orders in a roadshow cost nothing to place and nothing to withdraw, so the count measures how many investors want the option to decide on Wednesday, not what they have decided. The filed range still runs from $70 to $78, and the argument in the meeting rooms — whether Anthropic holds its lead against Google, and whether coding strength becomes knowledge-work strength — has not been answered by any number of orders. If the deal prices above the range, that is evidence. Until then, demand at an unstated final price is the weakest form of conviction a market offers.

Latest

Frontier · The trenches

Nvidia’s Board Sounded Out Arm Chief Executive Rene Haas About Succeeding Jensen Huang, Reports Say

The first named candidate for Nvidia’s top job is an outsider who used to work there: Arm’s Rene Haas, approached by the board, the Financial Times reports. Nvidia says no one has been formally approached and the search firm is not yet chosen. Both statements are now on the record.

Capital · The buildout

SpaceX Pledged More Than $74 Billion for Two AI Campuses, and Both Face Votes on December 9

SpaceX put a number on its next build on Thursday: more than $74 billion across Texas and Arizona, with the Arizona campus drawing up to 6 gigawatts — roughly the average power of five million homes. None of it is approved. Two local votes on December 9 decide whether the pledge becomes a project.

Frontier · AI security

OpenAI Launched Two Security Products: Agents That Attack Your Software, and Agents That Draft the Fix

OpenAI’s new security business has two halves: agents that break into your application on purpose, and agents that write the patch. Both launched Thursday. What the company has not published is any measure of how well either half works — no detection rate, no false-positive rate, no price.

Frontier · Beyond the giants

Q-CTRL Raised $290 Million to Sell the Software That Keeps Quantum Machines Working

The largest funding round yet for a quantum software company went to a firm that builds no quantum computer. Q-CTRL’s $290 million buys the layer that keeps other people’s machines accurate — and a navigation system for the places GPS cannot reach. It is now valued above $1 billion.

Frontier · AI security

Notion Confirmed Its AI Chat Transcripts Were Exposed in the Fireworks AI Breach

The Fireworks breach has a named customer. Notion says transcripts from fewer than 1% of its workspaces were taken from its model host’s systems — data Notion says should not have been kept at all, under a zero-retention commitment. The exposure sat two vendors away from the user.

Frontier · Infrastructure

The FAA Stopped Every Departing Flight in the United States for More Than Four Hours on Friday

At 3:54 p.m. on Friday, one advisory stopped every departing flight in the country. The cause was not an attack: communications failed across air traffic control centres running old equipment. More than 1,000 flights were cancelled before departures resumed at 8:15 p.m. The recovery runs into Saturday.

The Long View

One idea, at length

The Agents Are Being Shown the Door

United put AI agents on its list of prohibited ticketing practices this week, next to hidden-city fares, and said it can cancel a booking an agent made. eBay and Amazon have drawn similar lines. The argument is not about whether agents work — it is about who owns the customer.

Read the long view →

The Toolkit

Useful tools for the next generation of professionals — consumer and enterprise, tested by what they change about the workday, not by their launch posts.

Anthropic Lets Companies Run Its Agent Service on Their Own Servers, in Private Beta

Anthropic opened a private beta on November 12 for self-hosted Claude Managed Agents: the whole service that runs its agents — the server, the database that stores agents and session history, and the workers that run shell and file tools — installed inside a customer’s own cloud or data centre, instead of on Anthropic’s. The same programming interface as the hosted version applies, so existing integrations connect to the self-hosted server without a rewrite. Anthropic says it has no remote access to the server or its logs.

The boundary is worth stating plainly. The model does not move in-house: each request still goes to a model provider the customer chooses — Anthropic directly, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, or the customer’s own gateway — and Anthropic’s zero-data-retention terms apply to those calls as they do to other API calls. What the customer gains is control of the machinery and the record; what it takes on is the operations, including securing the setup (a PostgreSQL 16 or later database for persistent storage) and installing each release itself. Seven hosted features are missing at launch, among them webhooks, scheduled deployments and the Files API, per Anthropic’s documentation as reported. Access is through an Anthropic account team, for eligible organisations only, and no server price is published. This paper has not run the product. For a regulated firm whose objection to agents was where the session history lives, this is the first version of the product that answers it.

One tool earns its place each day. Novelty doesn’t.

Off the Radar
Evidence · Journal study

A Molecule Made by Gut Bacteria Healed Damaged Intestines in Mice and Human Cells

Some of the bacteria that live in a healthy gut make a small molecule that, in laboratory tests, switched damaged intestinal lining back into repair mode — speeding the regrowth of the surface that food, medicine and infection wear away. It has not been tested as a treatment in patients.

The full treatment →
Evidence · Journal study

A Newly Found Dinosaur Weighed About 400 Kilograms While It Was Still Growing Up

More than 200 million years ago, in what is now South Africa, a young dinosaur that walked on two legs already weighed as much as a grand piano — about 400 kilograms, or 880 pounds. Its near-complete skull is the earliest of its kind found in the country.

The full treatment →
Evidence · Journal study

A Tiny Brown Mushroom Is the First Found to Be Both Psychedelic and Deadly Poisonous

A mushroom small enough that several caps fit on a thumbnail has been found carrying two kinds of chemistry that were thought never to meet: the psychedelic compound in “magic mushrooms,” and amatoxins, among the deadliest mushroom poisons. It looks like hundreds of other little brown mushrooms.

The full treatment →
Evidence · Emerging technology

A Company Says Its 145-Billion-Parameter Model Runs on a Laptop, and the Download Is Free

Most models of this size live in data centres. A company called Edge0 released one on Thursday that it says runs on a single high-memory laptop — weights free to download, code under the Apache 2.0 licence. Every performance figure is the company’s own.

The full treatment →
Evidence · Research disclosure

Changing Seven Tiny Parts of a Model Can Hide a Trapdoor in It

A model can pass every ordinary test and still carry a hidden instruction: do this when you see that word. Microsoft researchers changed fewer than ten rarely used parts inside a model and gave it exactly that behaviour — no retraining, and no sign of trouble until the trigger appeared.

The full treatment →
Evidence · Open-source release

NVIDIA Gave Its Agent Safety Software to a Neutral Foundation

Agents need rules they cannot talk their way out of. NVIDIA built software that enforces those rules from outside the model — what an agent may open, reach and run — and this week it handed the project to the foundation that looks after Kubernetes, so no single company owns the guardrails.

        About The Tomorrow Post

        The Tomorrow Post is a daily newspaper about the frontier — the models, markets and machines deciding what happens next. Its tagline is its standard: a newspaper for the digital age.

        What This Paper Is For

        Signal over noise

        Most days, a handful of developments actually matter. The paper's job is to find them, verify them, and say plainly why they matter — and to let the rest go. A smaller edition of true things beats a large one of almosts.

        Three readers at once

        Every story is written to serve an investor weighing what something is worth, a professional deciding what to use, and a curious reader who wants to understand. Money, use, wonder — if a story serves none of the three, it isn't signal.

        A record, not a feed

        Stories here are followed, not dropped. Developing stories keep their history in the open — assessments dated, revised, and answered for — and the paper builds knowledge from its own reporting, so each edition knows what the last one said.

        Measured by design

        No clickbait, no pop-ups, no engagement bait. The paper is built to be forwarded: it succeeds when a reader sends a story to a smart friend.

        How We Work, Briefly

        Every claim is sourced, and sources sit on the story page. Company claims are labeled as claims, figures carry their caveats, and unverified reports are marked as such. The paper is produced with AI tools and written under house bylines; the standards above apply to every line regardless. Corrections and tips: hello@thetomorrowpost.com. The Tomorrow Post is a newspaper, not investment advice.
